RC9 gives governed context retrieval more time on large repositories. One operation can use up to
30 seconds, including preparation and selection. An opted-in passage step gets the last five
seconds of selection, and managed Codex prompt hooks allow 40 seconds for startup and return.
The operation returns sooner when it finishes. An individual metadata request retains its
one-second cap.

- Metadata selection can send fuller bounded JEV batches concurrently through a shared local
  admission pool. Spending, task identity and source-sharing rules remain project-owned.
- The maintained source index extracts better literal declarations, test labels and lifecycle
  clues. Current prompts are retained before older task background. Cold captured files can
  supply bounded syntax spans without waiting for the index to warm.
- Projects may opt in to JEV passage questions. JEV judges captured, permitted source passages;
  code preserves required guidance, file order, exact source ranges and fallback when answers
  are missing or uncertain. Existing profiles do not enable the new questions automatically.
- Receipts separate preparation, metadata, passage, provider and delivery limits. A partial
  inventory or a missed proof range remains visible rather than appearing as complete coverage.

Frozen local development cases show improved mobile-library passage delivery. Three fresh source-grounded
cases delivered one of five proof groups with live JEV, the same count as the provider-free RC9
arm. Existing disclosure and spending limits prevented wider coverage in those cases. These
comparisons do not establish lower total token use, faster accepted work or general accuracy.

Adopt deliberately in each checkout. Confirm the effective linked-worktree hook source, review
host trust, and configure the DL03 passage questions only where source sharing is approved.
Local source and installed-package checks do not prove native host delivery, device behavior,
application acceptance or results in another adopter. Computer-use automation remains deferred.
